**🟦 AZURE INFRA**  

⭐ 1. **SAP container images retired – removal set for Oct 14 2026** – workloads still using the SAP data connector must migrate now or lose support.  
2. **Azure Red Hat OpenShift with hosted control planes enters public preview** – a fully managed control plane simplifies Kubernetes ops and reduces admin overhead.  
3. **Azure SQL preview adds soft‑delete for logical servers** – accidental server deletions can be restored, improving disaster‑recovery confidence.  
4. **PostgreSQL skills & MCP plugin preview** – AI coding assistants can now query Azure Database for PostgreSQL directly, speeding dev cycles.  
5. **Guided Copilot experience in VS Code for Azure apps** – a step‑by‑step workflow takes you from idea to deployed app, cutting trial‑and‑error time.  
🔗 [Azure updates](https://azure.microsoft.com/updates?id=571342)  

**🛡️ AZURE SECURITY**  

⭐ 1. **CISA retires Weekly Vulnerability Bulletin in favor of risk‑based pivot** – federal guidance shifts, so align your Azure patch‑management to real‑world risk.  
🔗 [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/cisa-retires-weekly-vulnerability-bulletin-in-risk-based-pivot/)  

**🔐 CYBER / SECOPS**  

1. **OpenAI admits its models scraped GitHub for leaked API keys** – highlights the danger of unintentionally training on sensitive credentials.  
2. **London property manager breach via Metabase Cloud exposed bank details** – enforce strict SaaS access controls and monitor data exfiltration.  
3. **US Coast Guard & FBI board oil tanker after suspected cyber intrusion** – reminds enterprises to harden OT networks and supply‑chain links.  
4. **AI‑security spending spikes as fear outpaces proven value** – evaluate ROI before inflating budgets on untested AI defenses.  
5. **Perplexity’s AI agents built a database but were barred from running it** – illustrates governance challenges when AI creates infrastructure.  
🔗 [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/openai-says-its-models-hunted-github-for-leaked-api-keys-during-training/)  

**⚙️ CLOUD & DEVOPS**  

1. **Study: developers are “AI‑addicted” and managers reward the behavior** – consider policy limits to protect code quality.  
2. **Human oversight shifting from writing code to defining requirements** – update review processes for AI‑generated outputs.  
3. **Consolidating duplicate Azure DevOps pipelines with parameters cuts maintenance** – a practical tip for large‑scale CI/CD estates.  
4. **Splunk prepares a second open‑source LLM for telemetry data** – could reshape log‑analysis tooling and cost structures.  
5. **AI agents from Perplexity built a database but weren’t allowed to run it** – underscores the need for clear AI‑infrastructure governance.  
🔗 [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/study-developers-are-addicted/)  

**🤖 AI SECTOR**  

1. **GitHub rewrites Copilot runtime in Rust, boosting safety and performance** – a signal that production AI services are moving to systems‑level languages.  
2. **Apple reportedly building a server packed with M‑series Ultra chips for AI** – may introduce a new on‑prem AI hardware option for enterprises.  
3. **Huawei targets Q1 2027 launch of Ascend 960DT chip to challenge Nvidia** – could affect cloud AI pricing and hardware roadmaps.  
4. **Instinct and Meta’s Muse add voice‑call capability** – expands conversational AI use cases for customer‑facing apps.  
5. **Google, Nvidia, Anthropic & Emerald AI seek 100 GW grid capacity for new data centers** – underscores the massive energy demand of scaling AI.  
🔗 [TechCrunch AI](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/17/google-nvidia-and-anthropic-w
spokenText:
Good morning! Here is your daily brief for today.

First, the latest Azure updates. Microsoft announced that SAP container images will be retired, with support ending on October fourteen, two thousand twenty‑six. Any workloads still using the SAP data connector need to migrate now to avoid loss of support. Azure Red Hat OpenShift is entering public preview with hosted control planes, offering a fully managed Kubernetes control plane that reduces operational overhead. In Azure SQL preview, a soft‑delete feature for logical servers has been added, allowing accidental deletions to be restored and improving disaster‑recovery confidence. A new preview for PostgreSQL skills and an MCP plugin lets AI coding assistants query Azure Database for PostgreSQL directly, speeding development cycles. Guided Copilot experience in Visual Studio Code now provides a step‑by‑step workflow to take you from idea to a deployed Azure app, cutting trial and error time.

On the security side, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has retired its weekly vulnerability bulletin and is moving to a risk‑based approach, so align your Azure patch management to real‑world risk. OpenAI disclosed that its models inadvertently scraped GitHub and captured leaked API keys, highlighting the danger of training on sensitive data. A breach at a London property manager through Metabase Cloud exposed bank details, underscoring the need for strict SaaS access controls. The U.S. Coast Guard and FBI boarded an oil tanker after a suspected cyber intrusion, reminding enterprises to harden operational technology networks and supply‑chain links. Spending on AI‑security solutions is rising faster than proven value, so evaluate return on investment before expanding budgets. Perplexity’s AI agents built a database but were barred from running it, illustrating governance challenges when AI creates infrastructure.

In cloud and DevOps news, a recent study found developers are becoming “AI‑addicted” and managers are rewarding that behavior, prompting a need for policy limits to protect code quality. Human oversight is shifting from writing code to defining requirements, so update review processes for AI‑generated outputs. Consolidating duplicate Azure DevOps pipelines with parameters can cut maintenance effort for large CI/CD estates. Splunk is preparing a second open‑source large language model for telemetry data, which could reshape log‑analysis tooling and costs. The Perplexity incident reinforces the importance of clear AI‑infrastructure governance.

Now moving to the AI sector. GitHub has rewritten the Copilot runtime in Rust, boosting safety and performance and signaling a move toward systems‑level languages for production AI services. Apple is reportedly building a server packed with M‑series Ultra chips for AI workloads, potentially offering a new on‑premise AI hardware option for enterprises. Huawei aims to launch its Ascend 960DT chip in the first quarter of 2027 to challenge Nvidia, which could affect cloud AI pricing and hardware roadmaps. Instinct and Meta’s Muse have added voice‑call capability, expanding conversational AI use cases for customer‑facing applications. Finally, Google, Nvidia, Anthropic and Emerald AI are seeking one hundred gigawatts of grid capacity for new data centers, underscoring the massive energy demand of scaling AI.

There are no major market headlines in today’s briefing.

Bottom line: Azure is tightening support timelines and adding managed services, security guidance is shifting to risk‑based models, AI development tools are becoming more robust and hardware‑focused, and energy demands for AI are climbing sharply.

That is your update. Have a great day!
